newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian government urges UES prepare debt issue.
newsitem.headline: Russian government urges UES prepare debt issue.

text.p: The Russian government has recommended national electric company UES prepare before July a plan to issue long-term securities this year, Interfax news agency said on Tuesday.

It quoted an order by the government, which has a majority stake in UES, as recommending that the securities be offered on foreign and domestic markets. It gave no details of the maturity but said the bonds should carry an "indexed coupon".
UES had announced that it intends to issue a Eurobond in 1997 but has not detailed its plans.
It operates the national electricity grid and wholesale market, has majority stakes in most regional electricity companies and has stakes in power plants as well.
A new team of government reformers has targeted UES for reform, criticising high power rates for industry, low rates for household consumers and enormous company debts.
First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said earlier that the government could increase its control over the company.
